pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/toast/Toast.tsx:22 Toast owns a second polite live region of its own, beside the two regions that app/layout.tsx already mounts through AnnouncerProvider (lib/announcer.tsx), so a toast receipt and an announcer message written in the same breath race across regions and one is dropped with no trace, which is exactly what the technique's 'components request announcements; they never own regions' rule and the announcer's own 'ONE WRITER' rule exist to prevent.

techniques.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/toast/Toast.tsx:22 The earlier re-announce defect is fixed: line 24 keys the text by seq, so an identical receipt now remounts. But the toast is still an out-of-band notification with its own region, outside the shell's drain queue in lib/announcer.tsx, so the cross-region last-write-wins race remains.

packages/ui/src/components/button/Button.tsx:67 Native button with a required label prop. Disablement is honest: the button stays focusable, reads as aria-disabled, and the press is cancelled (line 68). Toggle and Seg are native buttons with aria-pressed.

packages/ui/src/components/field/Field.tsx:40 Field, TextArea and Select all require a label, wired as aria-label rather than placeholder. A description is attached through aria-describedby (line 30). Toggle's count is voiced through SrOnly unless an explicit name overrides it.

packages/ui/src/components/fold/Fold.tsx:56 A Fold keeps its body mounted after the first open and hides it with the hidden attribute, which closes the visual and accessibility channels from one condition. A closed Toast fades to opacity 0 but also empties its text and unmounts its ledger chip, so nothing stays reachable.

packages/ui/src/components/toast/Toast.module.css:9 Under reduced motion the toast drops the rise and still appears, so the feedback is replaced rather than removed. The blanket rule in app/globals.css:358 is the single signal that zeroes every transition; Fold and LevelSheet also carry local guards.

packages/ui/src/components/seg/Seg.tsx:1 Seg and TabRail deliberately do not claim composite roles (radiogroup, tablist), so there is no half-implemented roving pattern. Each stop is a native button or link that does something. Field restyles its focus indicator (Field.module.css:5) rather than removing it. The --focus-line contrast was not measured.

pairs.registryProposal: keyboard-navigation-models ('Focusable implies operable': every stop that does nothing on activation is a defect) and primitive-level-a11y ('prefer focusable-but-inoperable with an explanation') conflict over a disabled control that keeps its tab stop, such as TabRail's locked tab with tabIndex=0 and no href. The standard should state that an aria-disabled stop which announces 'unavailable' is not a false affordance.
